Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — BrightBridge is excited to move from pilot to production for our clinical-documentation workflows. Before we finalize a private offer, procurement asked for clarity on two items that are blocking internal approvals:

1) Commit smoothing across clouds: our usage will be spread between AWS Marketplace and GCP Marketplace for redundancy. We expect month-to-month variability (~40% - 160% of baseline). Can Redwood support a smoothing window for the private-offer commit (so spikes/valleys average over a quarter instead of month-by-month)? If so, how does that change the committed list price and the private-offer discount tiers?

2) Channel crediting to our reseller: our reseller (CloudResell Partners) must receive an immediately-applied channel credit on invoices (not a delayed rebate). We need to understand the passback mechanics and whether Redwood can issue invoice-level credits for Marketplace private-offer transactions or whether credits are handled via downstream reseller settlement.

I've attached the RFP and our sku map to make the ask concrete. Can your team provide:
- A short note describing available smoothing/window options and examples (3mo vs 6mo vs 12mo)
- A sample invoice flow showing where a reseller credit would appear
- Any contract language we should include to preserve the passback treatment

We are aiming to finalize commercial terms by the end of next week (30 Jun).

Thanks,

Hi Sam — great to hear and thanks for the clear ask. High-level answers below; I'll loop finance and channel ops for a short deliverable pack by EOD Thu.

Quick summary:
- Smoothing: we support a configurable smoothing/true-up window. Standard options are 3-month rolling average (default) and a 12-month true-up for large commitments. A longer smoothing window typically reduces the committed list price uplift (i.e., list stays closer to catalog) but requires a firmer annual commit for planning.
- Impact on discount tiers: because private-offer discounts are applied against committed list price, smoothing lowers monthly volatility used for tier calculation. For example (illustrative):
  - 3mo smoothing: baseline commit 1.0x -> eligible discount 15% at $X/month
  - 12mo smoothing: baseline commit 0.0x -> eligible discount ~17% at same annualized spend (absorb spikes)
- Channel crediting: we can support invoice-level credits for Marketplace private offers in two ways:
  1) Redwood issues an invoice credit to the buyer and offsets the reseller payment (preferred for bookkeeping clarity)
  2) Credits flow through the reseller settlement (reseller invoices/back-office) if marketplace constraints prevent buyer invoice edits

Ask from you: can you confirm the preferred mechanism (buyer invoice credit vs reseller settlement) and share a 3-month usage profile if available? That will let us model how smoothing changes the effective unit price.

I've attached a template showing how we typically structure passbacks and sample contract language for the invoice-credit option.

Next steps:
- Ben, Laura: can you prepare a short note (1-pager) contrasting 3mo vs 12mo smoothing and a sample invoice layout for buyer-credit vs reseller-settlement by Thu 24 Jun?
- Sam: if you can send a quick monthly forecast or confirm buyer-credit preference, we'll include a worked example for BrightBridge.

Best,

--

Thanks Soojin — buyer invoice credit is our preference (helps internal accounting). I've attached a short monthly forecast for the next 6 months; numbers are scoped to the clinical-doc pipeline (non-prod excluded).

A couple clarifying Qs:
- Our reseller (CloudResell) needs an explicit line on the invoice showing the channel credit and a unique settlement reference for reconciliation. Can Redwood include that on Marketplace invoices?
- If you do invoice credits, will Redwood provide a monthly passback report for the reseller showing applied credits + invoice references? We need that for our third-party audit.

If buyer invoice credits are not possible on GCP's marketplace path, we'll accept a reseller settlement but need the passback report guarantee.

Sam

Proposal (draft):
- Offer 3mo rolling smoothing as baseline for private offer; optional 12mo true-up at +1% list uplift but with stronger annual commit and 60-day notice for capacity planning.
- For AWS Marketplace: we can issue buyer invoice credits and show a distinct reseller credit line (passback) on the invoice. We will produce a monthly passback CSV containing invoice id, passback line item, reseller id.
- For GCP Marketplace: due to technical constraints, buyer invoice credits are not consistently editable post-sale. We recommend reseller settlement via CloudResell plus a monthly passback report from Redwood that mirrors the AWS format for reconciliation. Contract clause will guarantee monthly passback reporting and settlement timeline (Net-30 to reseller).
